A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ChatR1 and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Renumbered tables, appendix sections, and qualitative examples can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original conversational QA experiments across five datasets, retrieval evaluations, reward ablations, transfer results, and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds query-diversity, optimizer, rewrite-quality, and retrieval-system experiments.

M1.justification: v2 adds an evaluated GRPO-trained ChatR1 variant, whereas v1 uses PPO and lists GRPO as future work. The main reasoning/search procedure, composite intent-and-answer reward, and default PPO formulation remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The five datasets and existing cross-dataset transfer coverage remain unchanged. Table 8 adds tool-transfer scenarios on TopiOCQA and QReCC: models trained with dense retrieval encounter BM25 or dense retrieval with reranking during inference. Newly documented INSCIT filtering does not establish that coverage actually changed between versions.

E2.justification: The comparator rosters in Table 3 and the matched retrieval table remain unchanged. New comparisons evaluate GRPO against PPO-trained ChatR1 and BM25 or reranked retrieval against the default dense-retrieval configuration.

E3.justification: v2 adds experimental protocols varying the optimizer, rewrite-label source, and inference-time retriever, plus a query-overlap diagnostic. Reported INSCIT train/test turn counts change from 1,844/3,330 in v1 Table 7 to 1,443/2,767 in v2 Table 11; accompanying text specifies 2,197 filtered test turns. These reporting revisions do not establish that the retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 adds query-diversity analysis, PPO-versus-GRPO stability and performance tests, rewrite-quality sensitivity, and retriever-transfer tests. Conversely, v1 Appendix B's learning curves with versus without intent reward are removed; v2 Figure 8 answers a different question. Existing reward-weight ablations, first-search analysis, and qualitative examples remain.

E5.justification: Table 3 retains the same paired t-test reporting and p < 0.05 threshold. v2 introduces no new seed counts, repeated-run reporting, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures for its added analyses.

E6.justification: Table 3 and the matched retrieval table retain their numerical results, while Tables 4 and 6–8 add substantial new findings. For example, TopiOCQA F1 is 32.9 with GRPO versus 29.4 with PPO; ChatR1-3B with dense, BM25, and reranked retrieval scores 29.4, 17.6, and 31.8 respectively. These are comparisons across experimental variants, alongside new query-overlap and rewrite-quality results.

T1.justification: The problem definitions and Equations 1–10 retain the same mathematical content, including the reward definitions, PPO objective, advantage formulation, and critic loss. The PPO appendix moves from F to E; the GRPO experiments introduce no new formal derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: RL-based conversational reasoning and retrieval, an intent-aware reward, strong five-dataset performance, and cross-domain generalization. The additional experiments support and qualify these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning query exploration, GRPO's stability-versus-performance tradeoff, dependence on rewrite quality, and greater 7B robustness to retriever replacement. The limitations now acknowledge PPO/GRPO and describe moderate dialogue lengths as 10–20 rather than 10–12 turns. Existing explanations of intent rewards and retrieval-dependent answer quality remain.

D1.justification: v2 supplies ChatR1-specific code, dataset, and checkpoint access locations, replacing reliance on upstream implementation links alone. It also documents INSCIT clarification filtering, expansion of training references, and maximum-F1 scoring across gold answers. However, removing the ethical-considerations section also removes v1's approximately 1,500 H100 GPU-hour estimate; the hardware configuration remains documented.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including Gohsen et al. (2025), Lupart et al. (2025b), Yu et al. (2021), and Shao et al. (2024), modestly extending the surrounding literature and GRPO context. The central positioning against static supervised pipelines remains. The multi-aspect query-generation reference receives a publication update rather than representing a newly cited work.

P1.justification: There is distributed copyediting, clearer method wording, terminology standardization, and limited structural revision. Acknowledgements move, the ethical-considerations section and training-curves appendix disappear, and subsequent appendices are renumbered. The main narrative organization remains recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 adds four analysis tables and a two-panel PPO/GRPO figure while removing the original intent-reward training figure. Figure 7 changes from overlaid bars with gain annotations to side-by-side bars with absolute values; its intermediate ticks change from 0.5/0.33 to 0.631/0.5 while retaining the MRR@3 label. Existing tables and appendix displays are also renumbered and repositioned.

improvement.justification: The new optimizer, rewrite-quality, and retriever-transfer studies provide useful checks beyond v1's evidence, while INSCIT processing details and resource access instructions improve reproducibility. The net gain is limited by removal of the intent-reward learning curves and compute estimate, inconsistent INSCIT counts, the query-diversity analysis's unexplained >2-query condition despite a two-call limit, and Figure 7's ambiguous axis relabeling.
